# Movement data {orientation="columns"}

## {.sidebar .fill}

**Upload data**

```{r}
actionButton("use_demo_data", "Use demo dataset", class = "btn-primary")
br()
fileInput("uploaded_data", "...or upload your own CSV",
          accept = ".csv")
hr()
selectInput("id",     "Caribou:", choices = character(0))
selectInput("season", "Season:",  choices = "Annual", selected = "Annual")
sliderInput("year_range", "Years:", min = 2000, max = 2001,
            value = c(2000, 2001), step = 1, sep = "")
hr()
radioButtons("map_mode", "Map view:",
             choices  = c("Static points & tracks" = "static",
                          "Animation"               = "animation"),
             selected = "static")

hr()
conditionalPanel(
  condition = "input.map_mode == 'static'",
  sliderInput("alpha", "Opacity:",   min = 0, max = 1,  value = 0.5, step = 0.1),
  sliderInput("size",  "Point size:", min = 0, max = 10, value = 1,   step = 1)
)
conditionalPanel(
  condition = "input.map_mode == 'animation'",
  sliderInput("animation_index", "Time Step:",
              min = 1, max = 100, value = 1, step = 1,
              animate = animationOptions(interval = 120, loop = FALSE,
                                         playButton  = "Play",
                                         pauseButton = "Pause")),
  uiOutput("current_time_label"),
  p(style = "font-size:0.8rem;color:#666;margin-top:4px;",
    "Click 'Play' to animate."),
  hr(),
  sliderInput("line_width", "Line width:", min = 1, max = 8, value = 3, step = 1)
)
```

## Column {width=75% .tabset}

### Mapview

```{r}
leafletOutput("map", height = "100%")
```

### Movement stats

```{r}
#| title: Individuals by season
tableOutput("individuals_by_season_table")
```

```{r}
#| title: Sampling duration
plotOutput("sampling_duration_plot")
```

### Help

**1. Load data.** Click "Use demo dataset", or upload your own CSV, in the
sidebar. This is the shared dataset used across the whole app — Seasonal
ranges and Seasonal paths both work from the same data.

**2. Filter the map.** Choose a **Caribou**, **Season**, and **Years**
range from the sidebar; these apply only to the **Mapview** tab and the
"Summary stats" card. The **Movement stats** tab (table and plot) always
summarizes every individual and year in the loaded dataset, regardless of
these filters, so you can see the full picture at a glance.

**3. Pick a map view:**

- **Static points & tracks** — plots the filtered relocations as points and
  connects them into tracks. Use the Opacity and Point size sliders to
  adjust how they're drawn.
- **Animation** — replays the selected individual's movement over time.
  Use "Play"/"Pause" or drag the Time Step slider to scrub through it, and
  Line width to adjust the trail. Every individual's starting location is
  also shown for context.

**4. Read the results:**

- **Mapview** — GPS points, tracks, and the population boundary (static
  mode), or the animated path and starting locations (animation mode).
  Toggle any layer on/off from the layer control in the map's top-right
  corner.
- **Movement stats** — a table of how many individuals were tracked in
  each season/phase by year, and a plot of each individual's sampling
  duration (first to last relocation, by year).
- The right-hand column shows **Summary stats** (season, years, date
  range, and relocation count for the current filter) in static mode, or
  **Animation details** (the current playback position and a map legend)
  in animation mode.

```{r}
#| context: server
source("R/server_movement.R", local = TRUE)
```

# Seasonal ranges {orientation="columns"}

## {.sidebar .fill}

**Select method**

```{r}
selectInput("id3", "Caribou:", choices = character(0))
selectInput("phase3", "Season:", choices = "Annual", selected = "Annual")
conditionalPanel(
  condition = "input.phase3 == 'Annual'",
  checkboxInput("include_migration3", "Include migration periods?", value = FALSE),
  p(style = "font-size:0.8rem;color:#666;margin-top:-8px;",
    "When checked, migration-period relocations are estimated separately ",
    "with a Brownian bridge (BBMM) and combined into the annual range; ",
    "when unchecked, they're excluded from the estimate.")
)
sliderInput("year_range3", "Years:", min = 2000, max = 2001,
            value = c(2000, 2001), step = 1, sep = "")
hr()
radioButtons("hr_method3", "Estimator:",
             choices  = c("MCP" = "MCP", "KDE" = "KDE", "aKDE" = "aKDE"),
             selected = "KDE")
sliderInput("levels3", "Isopleth level:", min = 0.5, max = 0.99, value = 0.95, step = 0.01)
conditionalPanel(
  condition = "input.hr_method3 == 'KDE'",
  sliderInput("h3", "KDE bandwidth multiplier:", min = 0, max = 1, value = 0, step = 0.05),
  p(style = "font-size:0.8rem;color:#666;margin-top:-8px;",
    "0 = automatic reference bandwidth; otherwise scales it.")
)
conditionalPanel(
  condition = "input.hr_method3 == 'aKDE'",
  selectInput("ctmm_model3", "Movement model:",
              choices = c("Brownian motion (BM)"        = "bm",
                          "Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU)"      = "ou",
                          "OU + velocity (OUF)"          = "ouf",
                          "Independent (IID)"            = "iid",
                          "Auto-select (AICc)"           = "auto"),
              selected = "iid"),
  p(style = "font-size:0.8rem;color:#666;margin-top:-8px;",
    "Autocorrelated KDE via Kriging of the fitted movement model. IID ",
    "matches classic KDE; OU/OUF account for autocorrelated movement; ",
    "Auto-select can be slow.")
)
hr()
actionButton("estimate_range3", "Estimate range", class = "btn-primary", width = "100%")
```

## Column {width=65% .tabset}

### Mapview

```{r}
leafletOutput("map3", height = "100%")
```

### Population plots

```{r}
plotOutput("range_by_id_plot3", height = "100%")
```

### Methods

An individual's seasonal or annual range is estimated from its GPS
relocations (filtered by the sidebar's Caribou, Season, and Years) using
one of three estimators:

- **MCP (Minimum Convex Polygon)** — the smallest convex polygon enclosing
  the selected percentage of relocations. Simple and fast, but sensitive to
  outliers and tends to overestimate range in irregularly-shaped areas.
- **KDE (Kernel Density Estimation)** — a smoothed utilization distribution
  built from a kernel placed at each relocation. Bandwidth defaults to
  `amt`'s automatic reference bandwidth; the "KDE bandwidth multiplier"
  slider scales it up or down.
- **aKDE (autocorrelated KDE)** — fits a continuous-time movement model
  (IID, OU, OUF, or AICc auto-selected, via the `ctmm` package) and
  estimates the range from a Kriged occurrence distribution. Unlike plain
  KDE, this accounts for the temporal autocorrelation inherent in regularly
  sampled GPS fixes, and is the more statistically appropriate choice when
  fixes are closely spaced in time.

All three produce a boundary at the selected **isopleth level** (default
95%) — the smallest area estimated to contain that percentage of the
animal's space use.

**Multiple years.** When the Years slider spans more than one year, each
year is estimated independently and the resulting polygons are combined
with a spatial union into that individual's overall range. This is why the
"Estimated areas" table shows one row per year plus a "Total" row, and why
the map/plots can show a separate dashed contour per year.

**Migration periods (Annual only).** Movement during migration is fast and
directional, not the stationary space-use that MCP/KDE/aKDE assume — so
when Season is "Annual", the **"Include migration periods?"** checkbox
controls how those relocations are handled:

- **Checked (default)** — migration-period relocations are estimated
  separately with a **BBMM (Brownian Bridge Movement Model)** — the same
  Kriged-occurrence machinery as the Seasonal paths page's Kriging method,
  fit with a Brownian-motion movement model — and the result is combined
  with a spatial union into the annual range alongside the selected
  estimator's result for the rest of the year. The migration-only polygon
  is also drawn on its own as the **Migration corridor** map layer, so you
  can see exactly which part of the annual range comes from migratory
  movement versus stationary space use.
- **Unchecked** — migration-period relocations are excluded entirely, so
  the annual range reflects only non-migratory space use, and no Migration
  corridor layer is drawn.

Either way, the "Estimated areas" table's **N** column always reflects
exactly how many relocations contributed to that row's area.

**Population level ("ALL").** Selecting "ALL" for Caribou repeats the same
per-individual (and per-year) estimation for every caribou in the current
filter, then combines the resulting individual ranges with a spatial union
into a single population-level range. Because a model is fit separately
for every individual (and year), this can take noticeably longer than a
single-individual estimate — especially with aKDE, and most of all with
the "Auto-select (AICc)" movement model.

### Help

**1. Load data.** Data is shared across the whole app — use the "Use demo
dataset" button or upload your own CSV on the **Movement data** page first.

**2. Set the filters.** In this page's sidebar, choose:

- **Caribou** — an individual, or "ALL" to estimate a population-level range.
- **Season** — "Annual" (no filter) or a specific season. Choosing "Annual"
  reveals the **"Include migration periods?"** checkbox (see the *Methods*
  tab) — checked by default, so migration-period relocations are folded
  into the annual range via a BBMM estimate; uncheck it to exclude them.
- **Years** — the year range to include.

**3. Choose an estimator.** Pick MCP, KDE, or aKDE (see the *Methods* tab
for what each one does). KDE and aKDE reveal extra options — a bandwidth
slider and a movement-model choice, respectively — only when selected.

**4. Set the isopleth level** (default 95%) with the slider.

**5. Click "Estimate range".** The estimate isn't recomputed automatically
as you change filters — press the button whenever you want to refresh it.
Estimating for "ALL", with aKDE, or with migration periods included, can
take a while; a notification appears while it's running.

**6. Read the results:**

- **Mapview** — the estimated range, plus GPS points, tracks, the
  population boundary, (when Season is "Annual" with migration periods
  included) an orange **Migration corridor** layer showing the
  migration-only portion of the range, and (when more than one year was
  estimated) a dashed contour per year. Toggle any of these on/off from
  the layer control in the map's top-right corner.
- **Population plots** — one panel per caribou, only shown when "ALL" is
  selected, for comparing individual ranges side by side at the same
  spatial extent.
- **Summary stats** / **Estimated areas** (right column) — a quick summary
  of the current selection, and a table of areas (km²) with one row per
  year plus totals.

# Seasonal paths {orientation="columns"}

## {.sidebar}

**Select method**

```{r}
selectInput("id4", "Caribou:", choices = character(0))
selectInput("phase4", "Migration:", choices = character(0))
sliderInput("year_range4", "Years:", min = 2000, max = 2001,
            value = c(2000, 2001), step = 1, sep = "")
hr()
radioButtons("method4", "Corridor method:",
             choices  = c("Line buffer", "Kriging (CTMM)", "Mixed approach"),
             selected = "Line buffer")
conditionalPanel(
  condition = "input.method4 == 'Line buffer' || input.method4 == 'Mixed approach'",
  sliderInput("buffer4", "Corridor buffer (m):", min = 100, max = 5000,
              value = 500, step = 100)
)
conditionalPanel(
  condition = "input.method4 == 'Kriging (CTMM)' || input.method4 == 'Mixed approach'",
  selectInput("ctmm_model4", "Movement model:",
              choices = c("Brownian motion (BM)"        = "bm",
                          "Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU)"      = "ou",
                          "OU + velocity (OUF)"          = "ouf",
                          "Auto-select (AICc)"           = "auto"),
              selected = "bm"),
  p(style = "font-size:0.8rem;color:#666;margin-top:-8px;",
    "Occurrence distribution estimated via continuous-time (Kriging) ",
    "interpolation of the fitted movement model. BM is the classic ",
    "Brownian bridge; OU/OUF account for autocorrelated movement; ",
    "Auto-select can be slow."),
  sliderInput("footprint_level4", "Corridor footprint level:",
              min = 0.5, max = 0.99, value = 0.99, step = 0.01),
  sliderInput("grid_res4", "Grid resolution (m):",
              min = 50, max = 500, value = 200, step = 25),
  p(style = "font-size:0.8rem;color:#666;margin-top:-8px;",
    "A finer (smaller) grid resolution is more precise but noticeably ",
    "slower, especially for \"ALL\" individuals."),
  conditionalPanel(
    condition = "input.id4 == 'ALL'",
    sliderInput("tier_moderate4", "\"Moderate use\" tier (% of population):",
                min = 5, max = 95, value = 25, step = 5),
    sliderInput("tier_high4", "\"High use\" tier (% of population):",
                min = 5, max = 95, value = 50, step = 5),
    p(style = "font-size:0.8rem;color:#666;margin-top:-8px;",
      "Population-level usage tiers (see the Methods tab) — only used ",
      "when \"ALL\" is selected for Caribou.")
  )
)
hr()
actionButton("estimate_path4", "Identify corridor", class = "btn-primary", width = "100%")
```

## Column {width=65% .tabset}

### Mapview

```{r}
leafletOutput("map4", height = "100%")
```

### Population plots

```{r}
plotOutput("corridor_by_id_plot4", height = "100%")
```

### Methods

An individual's seasonal migration corridor is identified from its GPS
relocations (filtered by the sidebar's Caribou, Migration, and Years)
using one of three methods:

- **Line buffer** — connects the ordered relocations for each individual
  x year into a track, buffers it by the "Corridor buffer" distance, and
  unions the buffered segments into a single polygon. Simple and fast,
  and follows the travelled path directly. When more than one year is
  selected, each year is buffered independently and the results are
  unioned into that individual's overall corridor — one row per year plus
  a "Total" row in the "Estimated areas" table, and a separate dashed
  contour per year on the map.
- **Kriging (CTMM)** — follows the Brownian-bridge population-corridor
  workflow used by Sawyer et al. (2009), the Wyoming Migration Initiative's
  Migration Mapper, and similar studies:
    1. A continuous-time movement model (Brownian motion, OU, OUF, or
       AICc auto-selected, via the `ctmm` package) is fit separately for
       each individual x year, and a Kriged occurrence-distribution
       surface is estimated from it on one shared spatial grid covering
       the full current selection, so every individual/year is directly
       comparable. Gaps of 8 hours or more between fixes are excluded from
       the bridging.
    2. Each year's surface is rescaled to sum to 1 (a proper probability
       surface), independent of relocation count or migration duration.
    3. An individual's rescaled yearly surfaces are averaged together and
       rescaled again, so an individual tracked over many years doesn't
       dominate the signal — one averaged surface per individual rather
       than a separate estimate per year (the "Estimated areas" table
       shows one row spanning the year range for a multi-year individual,
       and no per-year map contour, since the years are no longer kept
       separate at this point).
    4. That individual's migration-route footprint is extracted as the
       99% isopleth of their averaged surface.
  - For a single caribou, this footprint *is* the corridor. For "ALL",
    Steps 5-6 continue: each individual's footprint is rasterized to the
    shared grid and the population's footprints are stacked, counting how
    many individuals cover each pixel; the stacked count is then
    classified into three usage tiers — *any use* (>=1 individual),
    *>=25% of the population*, and *>=50% of the population* — each drawn
    as its own toggleable map layer and table row. With few individuals in
    the current selection, 25% may round down to the same "at least one"
    threshold as *any use*, so the Low and Moderate tiers can coincide.
- **Mixed approach** — the spatial union of the Line buffer corridor and
  the Kriging workflow's *any use* footprint, combining both perspectives
  into one polygon (per individual, and again across individuals for
  "ALL"). The population usage tiers above only apply to the Kriging
  method on its own.

**Population level ("ALL").** Selecting "ALL" for Caribou repeats the
per-individual corridor identification for every caribou in the current
filter, then combines the individual corridors as described above. A
model is fit separately for every individual (and, for Line buffer/Mixed,
every year) with Kriging/Mixed, so this can take noticeably longer than a
single-individual estimate — especially with the "Auto-select (AICc)"
movement model.

### Help

**1. Load data.** Data is shared across the whole app — use the "Use demo
dataset" button or upload your own CSV on the **Movement data** page first.

**2. Set the filters.** In this page's sidebar, choose:

- **Caribou** — an individual, or "ALL" to identify a population-level
  corridor.
- **Migration** — the migration period to include (only migration-period
  relocations are used, since corridors describe movement between ranges).
- **Years** — the year range to include.

**3. Choose a corridor method.** Pick Line buffer, Kriging (CTMM), or
Mixed approach (see the *Methods* tab for what each one does). Line buffer
reveals a buffer-distance slider; Kriging and Mixed reveal a movement-model
choice — only when relevant.

**4. Click "Identify corridor".** The corridor isn't recomputed
automatically as you change filters — press the button whenever you want
to refresh it. Estimating for "ALL" or with Kriging can take a while; a
notification appears while it's running.

**5. Read the results:**

- **Mapview** — the identified corridor, plus GPS points, tracks, the
  population boundary, and (when more than one year was estimated with
  Line buffer or Mixed) a dashed contour per year. With Kriging and "ALL"
  selected, the corridor is shown as three separate usage-tier layers
  ("any use" through ">=50% of population") instead of a single fill.
  Toggle any of these on/off from the layer control in the map's top-right
  corner.
- **Population plots** — one panel per caribou, only shown when "ALL" is
  selected, for comparing individual corridors side by side at the same
  spatial extent.
- **Summary stats** / **Estimated areas** (right column) — a quick summary
  of the current selection, and a table of areas (km²) with one row per
  year (Line buffer/Mixed) or per multi-year average (Kriging), plus
  totals and, for Kriging with "ALL", one row per usage tier.
